Auckland FC captain Hiroki Sakai is staying cool as the rest of the A-League are trying to hunt the Black Knights down following their heavy defeat to Western Sydney Wanderers. 
 The New Zealand-based side suffered their first loss of the season in a 5-2 thumping 
 from the Wanderers and their heaviest defeat since a 4-2 loss to the now-defunct Western United in May 2025. 
 Sakai remained calm speaking before his side’s fixture against the Brisbane Roar and said he felt no different despite the suggestion other clubs were out to hunt down last season’s champions. 
 “It’s the same feeling [as last season],” Sakai said. 
 “Actually Western Sydney Wanderers was very good and the stadium also [had a] big crowd and especially for their first home game. 
 Advertisement Advertise with NZME. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. “That’s why yeah, of course we’re all disappointed a little bit. But as I said, we have to ... have a good reaction after that kind of bad game.”
 Hiroki Sakai captained Auckland FC in their 5-2 loss to the Western Sydney Wanderers. Photo / Photosport Auckland FC have undergone several major changes coming into the season, including Pedro Moreira replacing Steve Corica as coach, with Sakai suggesting the team are still developing into the new system.
 “We changed a lot, but we have to adapt to the new style and we need to develop more, it means develop our performance and our tactics and especially our results also.”
 Advertisement Advertise with NZME. The Black Knights go into their Brisbane fixture without last season’s top goalscorer Sam Cosgrove, after he was handed a one-game ban by Football Australia for failing “to uphold the expected standards of integrity, dignity and professionalism required of a professional player”.
 The 29-year-old was involved in a verbal altercation with Stuff reporter Andrew Voerman over a line of questioning regarding the club finding a way to have him serve a suspension picked up against Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli during the Fifa Intercontinental Cup in August outside of the A-League.
 The suspension also comes with a $2000 fine, but the striker will be available for selection against the Wellington Phoenix in next week’s derby in Auckland.
 Samuel Sherry is a live news sport journalist for the New Zealand Herald , based in Auckland.
